_comment: TTS-INPUT SUBSTITUTION ONLY. Read this before touching this file. These respellings exist ONLY to fix ElevenLabs mispronunciation of Texas place names -- they are substituted into the text sent to the TTS API inside scripts/gen-listing-voiceover.py and NOWHERE else. NEVER apply this map to on-screen text, captions, social post copy, or anything a human reads -- the correct spelling ('Boerne', 'Bexar', etc.) must stay everywhere except the literal TTS input string. Each entry only exists because it was researched (see 'source') or directly confirmed by Heath -- do not add a guessed respelling; leave it out and flag it instead per CLAUDE.md operating discipline.

entries.note: Heath confirmed directly, 2026-09-12: pronounced BURN-ee. Caused the Wild Cherry (104 Wild Cherry, Boerne) voiceover to mispronounce it phonetically. Highest-priority entry -- affects every future Hill Country listing near Boerne.
Bexar County (San Antonio). Locally pronounced 'BAIR' -- the X is silent, not read literally. Confirmed via bexar.org FAQ and multiple local sources.
Coastal-bend town. Local pronunciation departs from standard Spanish ('reh-FOO-hyoh') -- residents say 'ruh-FYUR-ee-oh', and the town itself has embraced this on its welcome sign.
Gulf coast town. Local English pronunciation, not the Spanish 'pah-LAH-see-ohs'.
Hays County town south of Austin. NOT 'BOO-duh'.
Hill Country town/county/river. Texans say 'LAN-oh', not the Spanish 'YAH-no'.
Central Texas town (Limestone County). One of the most commonly cited Texas mispronunciation traps.
Historic New Braunfels district. German origin ('gruen' = green), pronounced exactly like the English word 'green'.
East Texas city. Local pronunciation drops the literal spelling's harder vowels in favor of 'nack-uh-DOH-chess'.
NW Bexar County town, part of Heath's San Antonio market. 'huh-LOH-tiss', not a literal Spanish reading.

Comal County town north of San Antonio, in Heath's Hill Country market. Sources agree on 'buul-VUR-dee' (stress on middle syllable); marked medium because the exact vowel in the last syllable varies slightly by source.

Comal County/River (New Braunfels area). Correct is 'KOH-mal' (rhymes with 'pal'); commonly mispronounced as 'KOH-muhl'. Included because it's a documented trap for non-locals, but marked medium since the standard English reading of the spelling may already land close to correct.

FLAGGED, NOT VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION. Historically pronounced 'man-SHACK' by Austin locals despite the Spanish-style spelling. But the road was OFFICIALLY RENAMED to 'Menchaca' in 2019, changing the correct pronunciation to 'men-CHAH-kah' for the current legal name. Left in the map at low confidence for the old/colloquial 'Manchaca' spelling only -- if a script ever uses the current legal name 'Menchaca,' do NOT apply this entry; that spelling should be read as 'men-CHAH-kah' via normal TTS, not respelled.

researched_but_excluded.confirmed_pronunciation: DOSS-ee -- rhymes with 'bossy'. First syllable 'doss', second a short 'ee'. Heath confirmed directly, 2026-09-16.
researched_but_excluded.reason: CONFIRMED PRONUNCIATION, DELIBERATELY NO SUBSTITUTION. The brand name really was coming out wrong ('DAW-see') in the Dossie D1 render, but the cause was the MODEL AND VOICE SETTINGS, not the spelling. That render used a non-approved config (turbo/multilingual at stability 0.5 / style 0.15); Heath's clone is approved at eleven_v3, stability 0.3, style 0.4 (heath-voice-clone-settings-locked.md). Once gen-listing-voiceover.py was fixed to actually apply that locked config, 'Dossie' spelled normally comes out correct and no respelling is needed. Measured, not assumed -- see 'measured' below.
researched_but_excluded.measured: Cosine similarity of the first-syllable vowel spectrum (40ms nucleus, Hamming-windowed DFT 150-3500Hz, cepstrally smoothed) against same-render rhyme controls 'bossy' and 'posse'. Control-vs-control ceiling (same vowel, different consonant) = 0.870. OLD config 'Dossie' = 0.581/0.610 -- a different vowel. NEW config (eleven_v3 + locked settings) 'Dossie' = 0.784/0.881 -- at the ceiling, i.e. the same vowel as 'bossy'. ElevenLabs scribe_v1 agrees: the old render transcribes as 'Dawsey', the new one as 'dossy'.
researched_but_excluded.do_not_add: Do NOT add a respelling entry for Dossie. The obvious candidates were tested in the same render and are WORSE than the plain spelling: 'Dossee' scored 0.386/0.532 and 'Dossy' 0.361/0.422 against the controls, and scribe_v1 heard both as the three-syllable word 'dossier'. If a future render mispronounces the brand name again, check the model and voice settings FIRST -- a respelling here is the wrong lever and makes it worse.

researched_but_excluded.reason: Common enough word (county/river/street name) that eleven_multilingual_v2 reads it correctly by default in spot checks. No confirmed mispronunciation incident. Left out per the 'don't guess, don't fix what isn't broken' rule -- add it if a real render surfaces a problem.
Standard Spanish word TTS renders correctly by default ('BLAN-koh'). No incident.
